Part A · Units and the SI system

A number without a unit means nothing

Slide 03 / 48
  • Physics is a science of measurement — every law is tested by numbers, and a result without a unit is not a result.
  • “5” is not a measurement — “5 m” and “5 kg” are. The unit is what gives the number meaning.
  • Five ideas build the chapter — units, measurement, errors, significant figures, dimensions.Each one answers a different question about the same reading.
  • The question behind all of it — how big is it, how sure are we, and how should we write what we know?
Chapter map

1 Units what we compare against

2 Measurement how we compare

3 Errors how wrong we could be

4 Significant figures how many digits we may write

5 Dimensions what kind of quantity it is

Teacher

Dosto, Physics ka matlab hai naapna aur samajhna. Aaj hum seekhenge ki naapte kaise hain, kitna sahi naapte hain, aur number ko likhte kaise hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements03
Part A · Slide 2 of the chapter

Every measurement is a number times a unit

Slide 04 / 48
  • Physical quantity — anything that can be measured and used in a law of physics: length, mass, force, current.
  • Measurement — comparing that quantity with a standard of the same kind.
  • Unit — the standard used for the comparison. The comparison is the measurement.
  • Number and unit move in opposite directions — a bigger unit gives a smaller number, because the quantity itself has not changed.
  • One length, two honest descriptions — 1 m = 100 cm: the same table, written with two units.
Formula

Q = n × u

Q the physical quantity

n the numerical value

u the unit

n ∝ 1/u — double the unit, halve the number.

Teacher

Jitni badi unit, utna chhota number. Table wahi hai, bas naapne ka paimana badal jaata hai.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements04
Part A · Slide 3 of the chapter

Two kinds of quantity: base and derived

Slide 05 / 48
  • Fundamental (base) quantities — independent; they do not come from any other quantity. Their units are base units.
  • Derived quantities — built from the base ones: speed = length/time, force = mass × acceleration.
  • Derived units follow the same way — m/s, m/s², kg m s⁻² (newton), kg m² s⁻² (joule).
  • Why the split matters — seven base units can express every other unit in physics.
Lego blocks

Base L, M, T — the three block types

Built speed, force, energy, pressure

Rule a derived unit is a product of powers of base units

Force = kg × m/s² = kg m s⁻² — nothing new, only the blocks rearranged.

Teacher

Base quantity matlab building block. Baaki sab, jaise speed ya force, unhi blocks se bante hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements05
Part A · Slide 4 of the chapter

The world settled on one system: SI

Slide 06 / 48
  • Older systems — CGS (cm, g, s), FPS (foot, pound, second), MKS (m, kg, s). Each country used its own.
  • SI, established in 1960 — the Système International d’Unités, adopted by the 11th CGPM.The mole became the seventh base unit in 1971, at the 14th CGPM — not the system itself.
  • One system removes the confusion — a result from Patna and a result from Paris can be compared without conversion.
  • Two conversions worth memorising — 1 N = 10⁵ dyne, 1 J = 10⁷ erg.
Systems

CGS centimetre, gram, second

FPS foot, pound, second

MKS metre, kilogram, second

SI seven base units, worldwide

Teacher

Pehle har desh ka apna paimana tha, isliye confusion hota tha. Ab SI sabke liye common hai — ek hi bhasha.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and MeasurementsMemory string: L M T I Θ N J07
Part A · Slide 6 of the chapter

Radian and steradian measure angle, not length

Slide 08 / 48
  • Radian (rad) — plane angle, defined as arc length divided by radius, θ = s/r. One radian means the arc equals the radius.
  • Steradian (sr) — solid angle, defined as area divided by radius squared, Ω = A/r².
  • A full circle is 2π rad — a full sphere is 4π sr. Both are pure numbers.
  • Both are dimensionless — once called supplementary units; in the current SI they are derived, dimensionless units.
Conversions

1° 1.745 × 10⁻² rad

1′ 2.91 × 10⁻⁴ rad

1″ 4.85 × 10⁻⁶ rad

180° π rad

Teacher

Jab arc ki length radius ke barabar ho, tab angle ek radian hota hai. 180 degree matlab π radian.

Part A · Slide 8 of the chapter

Prefixes let one number span 10⁻¹⁸ to 10¹⁸

Slide 10 / 48
  • Write units, not words — symbols are never pluralised (10 kg, not 10 kgs) and carry no full stop.
  • Capital only for people — N, J, W, Pa are capital; m, kg, s are lower case. Full names stay lower case (newton, joule).
  • Temperature is K — never °K. There is a space between number and unit: 5 m.
  • One prefix at a time — 10⁻⁹ m is a nanometre, not a milli-micrometre.
The ladder

10¹² tera (T)

10⁹ giga (G)

10⁶ mega (M)

10³ kilo (k)

10⁻² centi (c)

10⁻³ milli (m)

10⁻⁶ micro (µ)

10⁻⁹ nano (n)

10⁻¹² pico (p)

10⁻¹⁵ femto (f)

Teacher

Kilo matlab hazaar, milli matlab hazaarva hissa. Bas prefix yaad kar lo, number apne aap aa jaayega.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements11
Part B · Slide 10 of the chapter

Length runs from 10⁻¹⁵ m to 10²⁶ m

Slide 12 / 48
  • Direct methods — metre scale to about 1 mm, vernier callipers to 0.1 mm, screw gauge to 0.01 mm.
  • Indirect methods — parallax, triangulation, echo methods, electron microscope, X-ray diffraction.
  • Ten to the power of ten — each step of the ladder is ten times the last, and the instrument changes with it.
  • Range of the universe — proton 10⁻¹⁵ m, atom 10⁻¹⁰ m, human 10⁰ m, Earth 10⁷ m, observable universe 10²⁶ m.
Ladder of lengths

10⁻¹⁵ m proton, nucleus

10⁻¹⁰ m atom (1 Å)

10⁻⁷ m virus

10⁻³ m ant

10⁰ m human

10⁷ m Earth

10¹¹ m Earth–Sun (1 AU)

10²¹ m our galaxy

10²⁶ m observable universe

Teacher

Proton aur universe ke size mein 10⁴¹ ka fark hai. Isiliye alag-alag tarike chahiye — ek scale se dono nahi naap sakte.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements12
Part B · Slide 11 of the chapter

Parallax turns a small angle into a huge distance

Slide 13 / 48
  • Parallax — the apparent shift of an object when it is seen from two different points.
  • Basis (b) — the distance between the two observation points. The bigger the basis, the better.
  • Parallax angle (θ) — the angle the basis subtends at the object, in radians.
  • The formula holds only for small angles — with θ in radians and θ ≪ 1 rad, the arc is almost a straight line.
  • Try it with one finger — hold it at arm’s length and blink each eye: it jumps against the wall behind.
Formula

D = b / θ

D distance to the object

b basis — separation of the two viewpoints

θ parallax angle, in radians

For a star, the basis is the Earth’s orbit: b = 2 AU.

Teacher

Dono aankhon se baari-baari dekho — ungli apni jagah badalti dikhegi. Wahi parallax hai, aur usi se door ke taare naapte hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements13
Part B · Slide 12 of the chapter

The Earth–Moon distance from a 1.9° shift

Slide 14 / 48
1

Read the data

b = 1.276 × 10⁷ m (Earth’s diameter), θ = 1° 54′ = 1.9°.

2

Degrees to radians

1.9 × π/180 = 3.316 × 10⁻² rad.

3

Substitute in D = b/θ

D = 1.276 × 10⁷ / 3.316 × 10⁻².

4

Answer

D = 3.85 × 10⁸ m — NCERT quotes 3.84 × 10⁸ m, within rounding.

Watch the units

60′ 1°

π/180 the only conversion you need

θ in rad otherwise D = b/θ fails

The commonest error is leaving θ in degrees — the answer then comes out 57 times too small.

Teacher

Minute ko degree mein badlo (60′ = 1°), phir radian mein. Yahi step sabse zyada galat hota hai.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurementsθ = 1° 54′ = 1.9°14
Part B · Slide 13 of the chapter

AU, light year and parsec each answer a different question

Slide 15 / 48
  • Astronomical unit (AU) — mean Earth–Sun distance, 1.496 × 10¹¹ m. Used inside the solar system.
  • Light year (ly) — the distance light travels in one year, 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m. A unit of distance, never of time.
  • Parsec (pc) — the distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond, 3.08 × 10¹⁶ m ≈ 3.26 ly.
  • Check the light year — c × 1 year = 3 × 10⁸ × 3.156 × 10⁷ ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.
The three units

1 AU 1.496 × 10¹¹ m

1 ly 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m

1 pc 3.08 × 10¹⁶ m = 3.26 ly

Sunlight to Earth takes 8 min 20 s; one light year is 63 000 times that distance.

Teacher

Light year time nahi, distance hai! Yeh sabse popular galti hai — exam mein bhi, interview mein bhi.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements15
Part B · Slide 14 of the chapter

Below a micrometre, we stop touching and start inferring

Slide 16 / 48
  • Angstrom (Å) — 10⁻¹⁰ m; about the size of an atom.
  • Fermi (fm) — 10⁻¹⁵ m; the size of a nucleus, a hundred thousand times smaller than the atom.
  • Electron microscope — electrons have far shorter wavelengths than visible light, so they resolve finer detail.
  • Other indirect tools — X-ray diffraction for crystal spacing, scanning probe methods for surfaces.
Small units

1 nm 10⁻⁹ m

1 Å 10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.1 nm

1 fm 10⁻¹⁵ m

Atom 10⁻¹⁰ m vs nucleus 10⁻¹⁵ m: a factor of 10⁵ — the atom is mostly empty space.

Teacher

Atom ko seedha scale se nahi naap sakte. Isliye electron beam ya X-rays jaise indirect tareeke use hote hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements16
Part B · Slide 15 of the chapter

Mass spans 85 powers of ten

Slide 17 / 48
  • SI unit — the kilogram, now defined by the Planck constant rather than a metal cylinder.
  • Atomic mass unit (u) — one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom; 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
  • How we weigh — mass spectrometer for atoms and molecules, balances for everyday objects, orbits and gravitation for planets and stars.
  • Other units in use — quintal (100 kg), tonne (1000 kg), carat (200 mg).
Ladder of masses

10⁻³¹ kg electron

10⁻²⁷ kg proton, 1 u

10⁰ kg 1 litre of water

10² kg human

10²⁴ kg Earth

10³⁰ kg Sun

10⁵⁵ kg observable universe

Teacher

Atom ke liye kilogram bahut bada hai. Isliye atomic mass unit banaya — ek carbon atom ke 12 hisson mein se ek hissa.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements17
Part B · Slide 16 of the chapter

The second is counted in caesium oscillations

Slide 18 / 48
  • The definition — 9 192 631 770 oscillations of the caesium-133 atom; an atomic clock is good to a second in hundreds of millions of years.
  • Why an atom — a pendulum wears, a quartz crystal ages, an atomic transition does not.
  • Range of time — light across a nucleus 10⁻²⁲ s, visible light period 10⁻¹⁵ s, heartbeat 1 s, a day 8.64 × 10⁴ s.
  • Big numbers — 1 year ≈ 3.15 × 10⁷ s; the age of the universe ≈ 4.3 × 10¹⁷ s.
Time values

1 day 8.64 × 10⁴ s

1 year 3.156 × 10⁷ s

1 shake 10⁻⁸ s

Age of universe ≈ 1.38 × 10¹⁰ y

Solar day ≠ sidereal day: astronomy uses the star-based day.

Teacher

Time naapne ke liye ek aisi cheez chahiye jo bilkul regular dolti ho. Atom sabse reliable hai — woh thakta nahi.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements18
Part C · Slide 17 of the chapter

Accurate is not the same as precise

Slide 19 / 48
Accuracy

Close to the true value

How near the measured value sits to the real value. Improved by removing systematic error — calibration, a better method, a corrected zero.

Precision

Close to each other

How near repeated readings sit to one another. Set by the resolution of the instrument, and improved by repeating and averaging.

The 100 g example

98.5, 98.6, 98.5 g precise, not accurate — a steady offset

99.9, 100.2, 100.0 g both accurate and precise

97.1, 102.6, 99.2 g neither

Four dartboards: tight at the centre, tight off-centre, scattered around the centre, scattered everywhere.

Teacher

Accuracy matlab sahi jagah, precision matlab ek hi jagah. Dono alag cheezein hain — ek instrument precise ho sakta hai aur phir bhi galat.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements19
Part C · Slide 18 of the chapter

Error has two natures: a bias you fix, or scatter you average

Slide 20 / 48
1

Systematic — instrumental

Faulty or uncalibrated instrument, zero error. Always in the same direction.

2

Systematic — method

Ignoring air resistance, a thermometer read too late. The procedure itself biases the result.

3

Systematic — personal

Parallax from a wrong viewing angle, a slow reaction time on a stopwatch.

4

Random

Unpredictable fluctuations of temperature, voltage, judgement. Reduced by repeating and averaging.

5

Gross

A careless slip — misreading a scale, writing 21 instead of 12. Fixed by care, not by statistics.

Least count

error ≈ ±LC

LC the smallest value the instrument can read

metre scale 1 mm

vernier 0.1 mm

screw gauge 0.01 mm

Teacher

Systematic error hamesha ek taraf kheenchta hai, random error idhar-udhar. Systematic ko sudharte hain, random ko average karte hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements20
Part C · Slide 19 of the chapter

Three numbers describe one measurement’s error

Slide 21 / 48
  • Mean of n readings — aₘ = (a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ)/n, taken as the best estimate of the true value.
  • Absolute error — Δaᵢ = |aₘ − aᵢ|, always positive, in the same unit as the reading.
  • Mean absolute error — the average of those, so the result is written a = aₘ ± Δaₘ.
  • Relative and percentage error — Δaₘ/aₘ (no unit), and × 100 for the percentage.
Formulae

Δaᵢ |aₘ − aᵢ|

Δaₘ (Δa₁ + … + Δaₙ)/n

relative Δaₘ / aₘ

percentage (Δaₘ / aₘ) × 100%

Pendulum readings 2.63, 2.56, 2.42, 2.71, 2.80 s → T = (2.62 ± 0.11) s, about 4.2%.

Teacher

Pehle average nikalo, phir har reading ka average se fark, phir uska average. Bas teen steps — aur sabse chhoti galti: absolute error ko negative likhna.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements21
Part C · Slide 20 of the chapter

Errors add by rule, and the power multiplies

Slide 22 / 48
  • Sum or difference — Z = A ± B gives ΔZ = ΔA + ΔB. Absolute errors add, because the signs are unknown.
  • Product or quotient — Z = AB or A/B gives ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B. Relative errors add.
  • Power — Z = ApBq/Cr gives p, q, r times the relative errors.
  • Exact constant — Z = kA gives ΔZ = kΔA: the percentage error does not change.
  • These are upper bounds — the true error is usually smaller, because some errors partly cancel.
Rules
OperationError rule
A ± BΔA + ΔB
AB, A/BΔA/A + ΔB/B
Aⁿn · ΔA/A
ApBq/CrpΔA/A + qΔB/B + rΔC/C
Teacher

Jodne-ghatane mein absolute error jud jaata hai, guna-bhaag mein percentage. Aur power ka error uske power se multiply hota hai — teen rules, poora chapter.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements22
Part C · Slide 21 of the chapter

Two resistors show how the rules combine

Slide 23 / 48
1

Series

R₁ = (100 ± 3) Ω, R₂ = (200 ± 4) Ω → R = 300 Ω, ΔR = 3 + 4 = 7 Ω.

2

Parallel value

R = R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂) = 100 × 200/300 = 66.7 Ω.

3

Parallel error

ΔR/R = 3/100 + 4/200 + 7/300 = 0.073, so 7.3%.

4

Parallel answer

ΔR = 0.073 × 66.7 = 4.9 Ω → R = (66.7 ± 4.9) Ω.

5

Power form

P = A²B³/(C√D) with 1%, 2%, 3%, 4% → 2 + 6 + 3 + 2 = 13%.

The trap

Series absolute errors add

Parallel product and sum in one expression

√D a power of ½, so 4% becomes 2%

C power 1, so 3% stays 3%

Teacher

Parallel wale sawaal mein dhyan rakho — product bhi hai aur sum bhi. Isliye dono rules lagenge. NEET isi type ka question bahut puchta hai.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements23
Part C · Slide 22 of the chapter

Five error questions, five traps

Slide 24 / 48
  • Q1 Z = A²B/C with errors 2%, 3%, 1% — the error in Z is?
  • Q2 R = V/I with V = (100 ± 5) V, I = (10 ± 0.2) A — find R ± ΔR.
  • Q3 Mass error 2%, speed error 3% — the error in ½mv² is?
  • Q4 Density = m/V, with radius known to 1% and mass to 1.5% — the error in density is?
  • Q5 A single reading from an instrument of least count 0.01 mm — what error do you quote?
Answers

Q1 2(2) + 3 + 1 = 8%

Q2 (10 ± 0.7) Ω — 5% + 2% = 7%

Q3 2% + 2(3%) = 8%

Q4 1.5% + 3(1%) = 4.5%

Q5 ±LC, i.e. ±0.01 mm

Teacher

Error wale questions mein pehla kaam — dekho quantities jud rahi hain ya guna ho rahi hain. Usi se rule choose karo, warna sab galat.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements24
Part D · Slide 23 of the chapter

Significant figures are the digits you actually read

Slide 25 / 48
  • Definition — the digits known reliably, plus the first digit that is uncertain.
  • A millimetre scale reads 4.23 cm — the 4 and the 2 are certain, the 3 is doubtful. Three significant figures.
  • A coarse scale reads 4.2 cm — two significant figures. Same object, less precision.
  • More figures means a finer instrument — not a better answer, and not a more accurate one.
  • Exact numbers never limit you — 12 oscillations, 1 m = 100 cm, the 2 in 2πr.
Read it honestly

4.23892 cm claims precision the scale never had

4.23 cm what a mm scale supports

LC 0.01 mm a screw gauge could write 2.345 cm

Significant figures report the instrument, not the arithmetic.

Teacher

Jo digits pakke hain plus jo pehla shak wala digit — wahi significant figures hain. Zyada likhna imaandari nahi, galat hai.

Zeros decide the count, and their position decides the rule

Slide 26 / 48
NumberSignificant figuresWhy
2343all digits non-zero
20074zeros between non-zero digits count
0.00252leading zeros never count
2.5004trailing zeros after a decimal point count
0.0502the 5 and the final zero

Teacher

Aage ke zeros kabhi mat gino, beech ke zeros hamesha gino, aur decimal ke baad ke zeros gino. Bas teen line mein poora rule.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and MeasurementsTrick: convert to standard form, then count the digits in front26
Part D · Slide 25 of the chapter

Standard form removes the ambiguity of trailing zeros

Slide 27 / 48
  • The form — a × 10ᵇ with 1 ≤ a < 10. 384 000 000 m becomes 3.84 × 10⁸ m.
  • Every digit in a is significant — so the notation fixes the trailing-zero problem for good.
  • Multiply and divide — multiply the multipliers and add the exponents; divide and subtract.
  • Order of magnitude — the nearest power of ten: multiplier below 5 keeps the exponent, 5 or more raises it by one.
Examples

4.7 × 10⁵ order 10⁵

6.3 × 10⁵ order 10⁶

0.000406 4.06 × 10⁻⁴, 3 s.f.

9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg electron, order 10⁻³⁰ kg

Some books cut at √10 ≈ 3.16 instead of 5; follow your textbook and stay consistent.

Teacher

Order of magnitude matlab ‘das ka kaunsa power sabse kareeb hai’. Isse electron aur Suraj ko ek hi line par rakh sakte hain.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and MeasurementsRound once, at the end — keep one extra digit in the middle28
Part D · Slide 27 of the chapter

Five rounds to the nearest even digit

Slide 29 / 48
  • Digit dropped is more than 5 — increase the previous digit by 1: 2.746 → 2.75.
  • Digit dropped is less than 5 — leave it: 2.744 → 2.74.
  • 5 followed by a non-zero digit — round up: 2.7451 → 2.75.
  • Exactly 5 with nothing after — round to the nearest even digit: 2.735 → 2.74, 2.745 → 2.74.
  • Round once — carry one extra digit through the working and round only the final answer.
Worked
NumberTo 3 s.f.
2.7462.75
2.7442.74
2.74512.75
2.7352.74
2.7452.74
0.0865 (2 s.f.)0.086
Teacher

Paanch se bada ho to upar, chhota ho to neeche. Aur bilkul paanch ho to — jo digit even hai wahan ruk jao. Rounding sirf last step par.

Leading zeros 0.00520 has 3, not 5

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements30
Part E · Slide 29 of the chapter

Dimensions describe the kind of quantity

Slide 31 / 48
  • Dimensions — the powers to which the base units must be raised to express a quantity.
  • Dimensional formula — the expression that shows them: force is M L T⁻².
  • Dimensional equation — the same statement as an equation: F = M L T⁻².
  • Independent of the system of units — which is exactly why dimensions can convert units.
  • Dimensionless quantities — strain, refractive index, relative density, plane angle. A radian has a unit but no dimension.
The seven

M mass

L length

T time

A electric current

K temperature

mol amount of substance

cd luminous intensity

Teacher

Dimension matlab ‘yeh cheez kaun-kaun se base units se bani hai aur kis power se’. Size nahi, sirf kism batati hai.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements31
Part E · Slide 30 of the chapter

Three steps turn any formula into a dimensional one

Slide 32 / 48
1

Write the defining formula

Force = mass × acceleration. Never start from the unit.

2

Replace each quantity

Acceleration → L T⁻², mass → M.

3

Collect the powers

ML T⁻² = M L T⁻².

Watch the denominator

speed M⁰ L T⁻¹

pressure M L⁻¹ T⁻²

h = E/ν M L² T⁻¹

G = Fr²/m² M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²

A quantity in the denominator takes the opposite sign of its power.

Teacher

Pehle formula likho, phir har cheez ki dimension rakho, phir powers jod do. Denominator ka sign ulta ho jaata hai — woh yaad rakho.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements‘Which pair has the same dimensions?’ is a yearly question34
Part E · Slide 32 of the chapter

Every term in a correct equation has the same dimensions

Slide 35 / 48
  • The principle — in a physically correct equation, the dimensions of every term on both sides are identical.
  • Only like can be added — you cannot add a length to a speed, so a mismatched term proves the equation wrong.
  • v = u + at passes — L T⁻¹ = L T⁻¹ + L T⁻²T.
  • v = u + at² fails — the second term is L, not L T⁻¹.
  • But consistency is not proof — s = ut + at² passes dimensions and is still wrong, because the ½ is missing.
Arguments must be pure

sin, cos, tan argument dimensionless

eˣ, log x argument dimensionless

ωt T⁻¹T = pure number

λt pure number, so N₀e⁻ᵏᵗ works

Teacher

Equation ke dono taraf ki dimension barabar honi chahiye — jaise tarazu ke do palle. Lekin dimension sahi hone ka matlab answer sahi nahi.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements35
Part E · Slide 33 of the chapter

Six checks: five pass, and one is a wrong version of a right formula

Slide 36 / 48
1

T = 2π√(l/g)

√(L/L T⁻²) = T — correct.

2

T = 2π√(m/k)

k = M T⁻², so √(M/M T⁻²) = T — correct.

3

v = √(P/ρ)

√(M L⁻¹ T⁻²/M L⁻³) = L T⁻¹ — correct.

4

v = √(F/μ)

μ = M L⁻¹, so √(M L T⁻²/M L⁻¹) = L T⁻¹ — correct.

5

F = mv²/r

ML² T⁻²/L = M L T⁻² — correct.

6

T = 2π√(g/l)

√(L T⁻²/L) = T⁻¹ — a frequency, not a period.

Method

1 turn every symbol into its dimension

2 simplify the right side to one bracket

3 compare the powers of M, L, T

4 state the comparison, not just ‘correct’

Teacher

Har symbol ko dimension mein badlo aur cancel karo. Match ho gaya to equation dimensionally sahi hai — bas itna hi, isse zyada nahi.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements36
Part E · Slide 34 of the chapter

Change the unit, and the number changes by the same powers

Slide 37 / 48
1

The principle

n₁u₁ = n₂u₂ — the quantity is unchanged, so the number and the unit move in opposite directions.

2

The formula

n₂ = n₁ (M₁/M₂)ᵃ (L₁/L₂)ᵇ (T₁/T₂)ᶜ, with a, b, c from the dimensional formula.

3

1 N → dyne

n₂ = 1 × 10³ × 10² = 10⁵ dyne.

4

1 J → erg

n₂ = 1 × 10³ × 10⁴ = 10⁷ erg.

5

1 g cm⁻³ → kg m⁻³

n₂ = 1 × 10⁻³ × 10⁶ = 10³ kg m⁻³.

Sanity check

smaller unit bigger number

1 Pa 10 dyne cm⁻²

10³ g 1 kg

10² cm 1 m

Teacher

Formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi — dimensional formula lo aur har base unit ka ratio uske power par laga do. Chhoti unit mein number bada hoga.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements37
Part E · Slide 35 of the chapter

Dimensions give the form of a relation, never its constant

Slide 38 / 48
1

Assume a product of powers

T = k mᵃ lᵇ gᶜ for a pendulum.

2

Write the dimensional equation

T = Mᵃ Lᵇ L T⁻²ᶜ = Mᵃ Lᵇ⁺ᶜ T⁻²ᶜ.

3

Compare the powers

a = 0; b + c = 0; −2c = 1 → c = −½, b = ½.

4

Read the result

T = k√(l/g), and experiment gives k = 2π.

5

Same method, a string

v = k√(F/μ) with a = ½, b = −½; theory gives k = 1.

What it cannot give

The dimensionless constant: 2π, ½, 1/4πε₀. Dimensions fix the powers, never the number in front.

Teacher

Teen unknown, teen equation — M, L, T ke liye alag-alag compare karo. Aur yaad rakho: dimension se sirf form milta hai, 2π nahi.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements38
Part E · Slide 36 of the chapter

Six things dimensional analysis cannot do

Slide 39 / 48
1

No constants

It cannot produce 2π, ½ or 1/4πε₀.

2

No sums

In s = ut + ½at² it cannot decide the coefficients or the terms.

3

No trig, exp or log

Relations like y = a sin(kx) are not products of powers.

4

No separation

Work and torque share M L² T⁻²; frequency and ω share T⁻¹.

5

Three equations only

More than three unknowns in mechanics cannot be solved.

6

No proof

A dimensionally correct equation can still be physically wrong.

What it can do

Check is this equation possible?

Convert units between systems

Derive the form of a relation

Find the dimensions of a constant

Teacher

Dimension ek powerful tool hai, lekin jaadu nahi. Constant nahi degi, sum wale equation nahi solve karegi, aur ek jaise dimension wali cheezein alag nahi kar sakti.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements39
Part E · Slide 37 of the chapter

Five dimensional questions, five traps

Slide 40 / 48
  • Q1 Dimensions of Planck’s constant — and which quantity shares them?
  • Q2 Which pair has the same dimensions: torque and energy, force and power, impulse and force, pressure and force?
  • Q3 If F, v and T are fundamental, what are the dimensions of mass?
  • Q4 Which relation is dimensionally wrong: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, v = u + at²?
  • Q5 Dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity?
Answers

Q1 M L² T⁻¹ — angular momentum

Q2 torque and energy, both M L² T⁻²

Q3 F v⁻¹ T

Q4 v = u + at² — the second term is a length

Q5 M L⁻¹ T⁻¹

Teacher

Dimension likhte waqt bracket zaroor lagao, aur poora base dimensions tak simplify karo. Aadha adhoora likha to examiner number nahi dega.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements40
Part F · Slide 38 of the chapter

Ten slips that cost marks every year

Slide 41 / 48
  • 1 SI ‘adopted in 1971’ — established 1960; the mole came in 1971.
  • 2 ‘Light year is a time’ — it is a distance, 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.
  • 3 Adding % errors for sums — absolute errors add; % adds only for products.
  • 4 Dropping the power In Z = A³, a 1% error becomes 3%.
  • 5 Leading zeros counted 0.0025 has 2, not 4.
  • 6 Rounding in the middle — keep one extra digit, round once.
  • 7 Significant figures on a sum — sums use decimal places.
  • 8 Unit slips ‘kgs’, ‘°K’, a full stop after a symbol, ‘5m’ without a space.
  • 9 Radian treated as dimensional — it has a unit, not a dimension.
  • 10 Matching dimensions read as proof — it only shows the equation is possible.
Teacher

Yeh galtiyan har saal repeat hoti hain. Inhe ek baar apni copy mein likh lo — exam se pehle sirf yeh page padhna kaafi hai.

Part F · Slide 39 of the chapter

Five NCERT numericals, worked end to end

Slide 42 / 48
1

Sphere, r = 2.1 cm

V = (4/3)πr³ = 38.8 cm³ → 39 cm³, two significant figures.

2

Cube, side 1.2 cm

V = 1.728 cm³ → 1.7 cm³.

3

5.74 g in 1.2 cm³

ρ = 4.8 g/cm³.

4

Pendulum accuracy

L = 20.0 cm ± 1 mm, 100 oscillations in 90 s ± 1 s → Δg/g = 0.5% + 2(1.1%) ≈ 3%.

5

Two resistors in series

(100 ± 3) + (200 ± 4) = (300 ± 7) Ω.

Where the marks are

formula written first

substitution with units

significant figures decided last

error stated as ±

NCERT ke numericals simple hote hain — asli marks significant figures aur unit mein hain. Answer ke saath hamesha unit aur sahi digits likho.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and Measurements44
Part F · Slide 42 of the chapter

Revision 2: significant figures and dimensions

Slide 45 / 48
Rule or toolStatement
CountingNon-zero digits count; inner zeros count; leading zeros never; trailing zeros after a decimal point count.
Exact numbersCounting numbers and defined conversions have unlimited significant figures.
× and ÷Keep the fewest significant figures among the factors.
+ and −Keep the fewest decimal places among the terms.
Rounding> 5 up, < 5 keep, 5 with a tail up, exactly 5 to the nearest even digit; round once.
DimensionsPowers of M, L, T (and A, K, mol, cd) in square brackets; F = M L T⁻².
HomogeneityEvery term on both sides of a correct equation has the same dimensions.
LimitationsNo constants, no sums, no trig or log relations, cannot separate equal dimensions.

NCERT Class 11 Physics · Chapter 1 · Units and MeasurementsNumbers are deck slides · 43 chapter slides, one split in two47

Measure, state the error, check the dimensions

Three habits carry this chapter into every later one — and into every numerical in the NEET paper.

Habit 1

Always write the unit

A bare number is not an answer. Convert only after the formula is written.

Habit 2

Say how wrong you could be

Quote ± with every measured value, and carry the error through the calculation.

Habit 3

Check the dimensions

Before substituting numbers, confirm both sides of the equation agree.
